title: POC weekly sync — Quantization INT8 vs FP8 results review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 and FP8 quantization runs. Team walked through latency/throughput deltas, memory improvements, and a small set of quality regressions; agreed on targeted follow-ups (larger eval set, A/B on canary dedicated nodes, KV-cache verification).
topics: Next steps: benchmarks and rollout plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dana (NovaScale ML), Marcus (NovaScale SRE), Evelyn (NovaScale PM)
---
[00:00] Jordan: Okay team, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: we want to go over the INT8 and FP8 runs we pushed last week, focus on quality deltas and perf numbers, and agree next steps.
[00:18] Dana: Sounds good, we got the spreadsheet you posted. Quick note — Marcus did some smoke tests in our staging cluster overnight.
[00:30] Priya: Great. I can share the drive link again, it's drive.google.com/quant-results-nova (note: link shortened in chat). The runs are: baseline fp16, int8 static, int8 per-channel, and fp8 hybrid.
[00:52] Marcus: Side note, I saw the model OOM on the 32k sequence test with fp16 but not with int8 — that was helpful.
[01:05] Priya: Right, memory dropped roughly 2.3x with int8 across the 24GB instance, and fp8 was similar but had slightly higher peak allocations in our GPU mem trace — we think kernel fusion isn't hitting the fp8 path yet.
[01:30] Evelyn: On quality, Dana ran the 400-prompt eval we agreed on. High-level: INT8 per-channel had 95% parity on automated metrics but about a 6% drop on our subjective answers (clarity/faithfulness) on the subset. FP8 hybrid was around 98% parity but with a couple odd hallucinations.
[02:05] Dana: Yeah I pulled some examples, I'll drop them in the doc. One was a date mis-ordering — probably numeric calibration.
[02:20] Jordan: That's useful. Can you paste one example now?
[02:26] Dana: Sure — prompt about quarterly revenue, baseline mentions Q4 FY23, int8 said Q2, fp8 still said Q4 but added an extra sentence that seemed made up.
[02:42] Priya: Those are classic calibration/rounding artifacts. We suspect per-token quantization noise accumulates on numeric contexts. We can try per-layer rescaling in the quant config.
[03:00] Marcus: Also, the end-to-end latency numbers — we saw 12% improvement for int8 under small-batch interactive (batch=1) and about 28% improvement at batch=8. FP8 gave 18% and 32% respectively. So fp8 wins throughput but has those weird hallucinations.
[03:28] Jordan: Good to record — so int8 is safer on quality, fp8 gives better throughput but has edge regressions.
[03:36] Dana: On hallucinations, are these repeatable across seeds or just flakey? We tried 3 seeds and saw the same issue twice.
[03:45] Priya: Mostly repeatable, which indicates a deterministic quantization mapping issue rather than sampling randomness.
[03:53] Marcus: One more infra note: our KV cache performance under int8 looked fine, but fp8 had higher cache miss penalty in the trace — I think due to conversion overhead between host/GPU. Could be how the runtime handles kv serialization for fp8.
[04:15] Priya: Good catch. We'll open a runtime ticket to check the fp8 kernel path + KV copy ops. Might be a suboptimal memcpy pattern.
[04:28] Jordan: Let's go through the spreadsheet rows — Priya, can you narrate the key columns?
[04:34] Priya: Sure: columns are model variant, tokens/sec, p95 latency, peak GPU mem, ROUGE-F1, human-fail-count (from our 50-sample check), and notes. Example: baseline fp16 tokens/sec 420, p95 280ms, mem 11.9GB. int8-per-channel tokens/sec 470, p95 245ms, mem 5.1GB. fp8-hybrid tokens/sec 500, p95 230ms, mem 5.4GB.
[05:10] Evelyn: So roughly 15-20% token/sec gain for fp8 vs fp16 and 8-10% over int8. But we care more about the human-fail metric — 50-sample check had 3 failures for fp16, 4 for int8, and 6 for fp8.
[05:30] Dana: Correct. We also ran downstream QA on a reranking task and saw int8 barely changed MRR, fp8 had a 1.7% drop.
[05:45] Jordan: Okay. Two threads emerge: (1) reduce fp8 regressions if we want to adopt it for throughput, (2) int8 looks like a conservative win on memory/cost.
[05:58] Marcus: For the POC ROI calc — do you have per-token cost numbers mapped to our committed GAU?
[06:05] Priya: We have rough cost deltas in the doc. With current committed rates, int8 would reduce per-token cost by ~38%, fp8 about ~45% — but this assumes identical SLOs. If fp8 increases incidents/failures, the ops cost could negate savings.
[06:28] Evelyn: Right, quality regressions translate to product risk. We need a guardrail.
[06:35] Jordan: On guardrails: we can propose a canary rollout on dedicated nodes with automatic fallback to fp16 or int8 on error thresholds. Redwood's routing policies can do that.
[06:48] Dana: That would help. Also want to understand how quantization interacts with function/tool-calling — does int8 break structured output?
[06:58] Priya: We tested some tool-call flows; int8 preserved JSON structure in our samples, fp8 had two cases where a trailing comma was added — likely tokenizer alignment after quant maps. More tests needed.
[07:15] Marcus: Another infra ask: can Redwood provide a small dedicated pool to run A/B? We prefer to isolate the test to avoid customer-facing impact.
[07:24] Jordan: Yes, we can provision a 2-GPU dedicated canary cluster for the POC for a week. I'll include pricing.
[07:33] Priya: Actionably, we should: (A) expand eval to 2k prompts including numeric/time-sensitive items, (B) run per-layer rescale with int8 and fp8 variants, (C) open runtime ticket on fp8 KV path, (D) schedule canary on dedicated nodes.
[07:53] Dana: Agreed. Also can we add a smoke test that compares token-level logits for baseline vs quant to help triage differences?
[08:02] Priya: Yes, we have a diff tool in the repo — I can run it and output top-k token deltas for the failing prompts.
[08:13] Jordan: Good. Any blockers?
[08:16] Marcus: Timing: we need the expanded eval results by next Tue to align with our roadmap sync. Also security wants to review the dedicated node config (SSO, KMS).
[08:28] Evelyn: I'll coordinate security docs.
[08:31] Jordan: OK let's recap and assign owners.
---
[08:45] Summary recap: FP8 gives best throughput but exhibits more quality regressions and a KV/cache overhead; INT8 is conservative with good memory savings and modest quality impact. Agreed next steps: expanded eval, kernel/runtime investigation, canary dedicated run, and token-diff traces.
[09:05] Dana: I'll upload the extended eval set and sample failure cases to the shared folder.
[09:12] Priya: I'll run the per-layer rescale experiments and the token-diff for the 50 failing prompts.
[09:20] Marcus: I'll prepare dedicated cluster request details and check SSO/KMS handoff.
[09:28] Jordan: I'll follow up with pricing and canary provisioning plan.
[09:35] Evelyn: Schedule follow-up — same time next week?
[09:38] Jordan: Yes, same time.
[09:40] End recording.

Notes: occasional transcription errors: "KV cash" seen in raw auto-transcript; "Redwood Dedication" mis-typing, some speaker labels merged by auto-system.
